Check: (2√15)2 = 4 × 15 = 60, and 2√15 ≈ 7.75, which is between 7 and 8.

items.prompt:
A grain of sand is about 0.000403 meter wide. In scientific notation, this is 4.03 × 10n meter.

What is the value of n?

mistakes.why: You counted the moves correctly but gave the wrong sign. The number is less than 1, so the exponent is negative.
You counted the three zeros after the decimal point. Count the moves: the point moves 4 places to get from 0.000403 to 4.03.
You counted all six digits after the decimal point. The point stops after the 4, so it moves 4 places.

Move the decimal point right until one nonzero digit is in front of it: 0.000403 → 4.03. That is 4 moves.

The number is less than 1, so the exponent is negative: 4.03 × 10−4, and n = −4.

Check: 4.03 × 0.0001 = 0.000403.

items.prompt:
A sheet of printer paper is about 1 × 10−4 meter thick. Suppose 5 × 105 sheets were stacked in one pile.

About how tall would the pile be?
why: You combined the exponents as 4 − 5 = −1. When you multiply, add the exponents: −4 + 5 = 1.
You divided the number of sheets by the thickness, which subtracts the exponents (5 − (−4) = 9). Height = sheets × thickness, so multiply.
You multiplied the exponents (−4 × 5). When you multiply powers of 10, add the exponents.
items.hint: Height of the pile = number of sheets × thickness of one sheet.
items.explain:
Height = (5 × 105)(1 × 10−4).

Front numbers: 5 × 1 = 5. Exponents: 5 + (−4) = 1.

Height = 5 × 101 meters, which is 50 meters.

Sense check: 10,000 sheets make a stack 1 meter tall, and 500,000 sheets is 50 times that many. The choice 5 × 109 meters comes from dividing instead of multiplying.

items.explain:
Parentheses: 1 − 4 = −3. Now: 33 − 2(−3)2 + √81 ÷ 3.

Exponents and roots: 33 = 27, (−3)2 = 9, √81 = 9. Now: 27 − 2 × 9 + 9 ÷ 3.

Multiply and divide: 2 × 9 = 18 and 9 ÷ 3 = 3. Now: 27 − 18 + 3.

Left to right: 27 − 18 = 9; 9 + 3 = 12.

The tempting wrong answer, −6, comes from multiplying 2 × (−3) before squaring.

items.prompt: Which expression has a negative value?
why: The parentheses make −3 the base: (−3)(−3) = 9. Two negative factors give a positive answer.
A negative exponent means reciprocal, not negative: 3<sup>−2</sup> = 1/9, a positive number.
Any nonzero number to the zero power is 1, even a negative base: (−3)<sup>0</sup> = 1.
items.hint: Evaluate each one. Find the base first.
items.explain:
(−3)2 = 9.   −32 = −(3 × 3) = −9.   3−2 = 1/9.   (−3)0 = 1.

Only −32 is negative. Without parentheses, the exponent touches only the 3, and the negative sign is applied after squaring.

The tempting wrong choice is 3−2, because its exponent is negative. A negative exponent makes a reciprocal, not a negative number.

items.prompt: Which expression is equivalent to (2a3)2 · a−1?
why: You did not square the 2. The outside exponent goes to every factor: 2<sup>2</sup> = 4.
You added the exponents in the power of a power (3 + 2 = 5), then 5 + (−1) = 4. A power of a power multiplies: (a<sup>3</sup>)<sup>2</sup> = a<sup>6</sup>.
You multiplied 6 × (−1). Multiplying powers with the same base adds the exponents: 6 + (−1) = 5.
items.hint: Square every factor inside the parentheses, then use the product rule.
items.explain:
Power of a product: (2a3)2 = 22 · a3×2 = 4a6.

Product rule: 4a6 · a−1 = 4a6+(−1) = 4a5.

Plug-in check with a = 2: (2 · 8)2 · 1/2 = 256 ÷ 2 = 128, and 4 · 25 = 128.

The most tempting wrong answer, 2a5, forgets to square the coefficient.

items.prompt: Evaluate 3−1 · 6 + 50.

mistakes.why: You treated 3<sup>−1</sup> as −3, so you got −18 + 1. A negative exponent means reciprocal: 3<sup>−1</sup> = 1/3, and 1/3 · 6 = 2.
You treated 5<sup>0</sup> as 0. Any nonzero number to the zero power is 1, so add 2 + 1.
You treated 5<sup>0</sup> as 5. A zero exponent gives 1, not the base.

items.hint: A negative exponent means reciprocal. A zero exponent gives 1. Multiply before you add.
items.explain:
3−1 = 1/3, so 3−1 · 6 = 6/3 = 2.

50 = 1.

2 + 1 = 3.

The tempting wrong answer, −17, reads the negative exponent as a negative number.

items.prompt: Evaluate ∛(−125) + √121.

items.explain:
∛(−125) = −5, because (−5)(−5)(−5) = 25 × (−5) = −125.

√121 = 11, because 11 × 11 = 121.

−5 + 11 = 6.

The tempting wrong answer, 16, drops the negative sign of the cube root.

√45 is between {{0}} and {{1}}.

7<sup>2</sup> = 49 is more than 45, so 7 is the upper number, not the lower one.

items.prompt: A bacterium is about 6.2 × 10−5 inch long. Write this length in standard form.

mistakes.why: You moved the decimal point to the right. A negative exponent means a number less than 1, so move the point to the left.
You moved the decimal point 6 places. The exponent is −5, so move it 5 places to the left.
You moved the decimal point only 4 places. The exponent is −5, so move it 5 places to the left.

items.explain:
Move the decimal point 5 places to the left, filling with zeros: 6.2 → 0.62 → 0.062 → 0.0062 → 0.00062 → 0.000062.

Moving the point to the right (620,000) would make a bacterium about 10 miles long.

items.prompt:
A national government spends about $1.8 × 1010 per year on highways. The country has about 6 × 107 residents.

About how much highway spending is that per resident?
why: You changed 0.3 to 3 without adjusting the exponent. Making the front number 10 times bigger means making the exponent 1 smaller: 0.3 × 10<sup>3</sup> = 3 × 10<sup>2</sup>.
You divided residents by dollars. “Per resident” means dollars ÷ residents, so the spending goes on top.
You multiplied the two numbers. “Per resident” means divide the spending by the number of residents.
items.hint: “Per resident” means divide the total by the number of residents. Then make the front number between 1 and 10.

Per resident = (1.8 × 1010) ÷ (6 × 107).

Front numbers: 1.8 ÷ 6 = 0.3. Exponents: 10 − 7 = 3. So far: 0.3 × 103.

Adjust: 0.3 × 103 = 3 × 102, so about $3 × 102, or $300 per resident.

items.hint: Parentheses first, then every exponent and root, then multiply, then add and subtract left to right.
items.explain:
Parentheses: 2 − 3 = −1. Now: 42 − 5(−1)3 + ∛(−8) × 3.

Exponents and roots: 42 = 16, (−1)3 = −1, ∛(−8) = −2. Now: 16 − 5(−1) + (−2) × 3.

Multiply: 5(−1) = −5 and (−2) × 3 = −6. Now: 16 − (−5) + (−6).

Left to right: 16 + 5 = 21; 21 − 6 = 15.

The tempting wrong answer, 5, comes from treating (−1)3 as positive 1.

vocab.def: The number or variable that is multiplied by itself in a power.
The small raised number that tells how many times to use the base as a factor.
An expression made of a base and an exponent, or the value of that expression.

A number that, when multiplied by itself, gives the original number. The symbol √ means the positive square root.
A number that, when used as a factor three times, gives the original number.
A whole number whose square root is also a whole number.

vocab.def: Any nonzero number raised to the zero power equals 1.
An exponent that tells you to take the reciprocal of the positive power. It does not make the number negative.
A way to write a number as a number at least 1 and less than 10, times a power of 10.
A number written out with all its digits, the usual way.
The number multiplied by a variable or by a power of 10.
The number you multiply by to get 1; for a fraction, flip the top and bottom. A negative exponent tells you to take a reciprocal.

Order of Operations

  1. Grouping: ( ), [ ], | |, fraction bar, under a root
  2. Exponents and roots
  3. Multiply and divide, left to right
  4. Add and subtract, left to right

Example: 20 − 2 × 32 + √25 = 20 − 18 + 5 = 7

Roots

  • √64 = 8 since 82 = 64; ∛27 = 3 since 33 = 27
  • ∛(−8) = −2; √(−16) is not a real number
  • Simplify: √72 = √(36 × 2) = 6√2 (largest perfect square)
  • Estimate: 25 < 30 < 36, so 5 < √30 < 6
  • √(a + b) ≠ √a + √b: √(9 + 16) = 5, not 7

Scientific Notation: a × 10n, 1 ≤ a < 10

  • Big number: positive exponent. 93,000,000 = 9.3 × 107
  • Small number: negative exponent. 0.000002 = 2 × 10−6
  • Count the moves of the decimal point, not the zeros.
  • To standard form: move the point right (+) or left (−).
  • Compare: exponent first, then the front number.

Computing in Scientific Notation

  • Multiply: multiply fronts, add exponents. (3 × 104)(5 × 106) = 15 × 1010 = 1.5 × 1011
  • Divide: divide fronts, subtract exponents. (2 × 1012) ÷ (4 × 106) = 0.5 × 106 = 5 × 105
  • Adjust: front smaller by 10 → exponent up 1; front bigger by 10 → exponent down 1.
  • TI-30XS: x2, ^, 2nd x2 for √, ×10n key; type parentheses for a negative base.

Top mistakes: 43 is 64, not 12; 2−3 is 1/8, not −8; 70 is 1, not 0; multiplying powers adds exponents, a power of a power multiplies them; square the coefficient too: (2x)2 = 4x2; small numbers get negative exponents; adjust the exponent when you fix the front number.
